title: A consumer migrated before the formatter exclusion existed never receives it, so its pre-commit formatter rewrites a view after the doctor gate, and one rewritten view refuses every later commit
body:
Raised by utilz-vc on hv's instruction, 2026-09-14, from Utilz, a consumer project then on intent 3.0.1.

## What happened

On 2026-09-14 Utilz's pre-commit doctor gate refused every commit, by every node, whatever the commit touched. Three issue views, `intent/issues/0025.md` to `0027.md`, were each one byte shorter on disk than the store rendered them: `0025.md` held 3384 bytes against 3385. Each stored body carried two blank lines before its `## Resolution` heading, and the renderer reproduced them. Utilz's own pre-commit block, `prettier --write` over every staged `.md` followed by `git add`, collapsed them to one after the doctor gate had passed. So the commit that closed the three issues (Utilz `387e377`) landed views the store disagreed with, and from then on the doctor gate found the skew and refused every commit. Utilz fixed the three bodies through `intent issues edit` at `895a2fc`, one byte each.

## Why the formatter could reach the views

- **The exclusion exists and never reached this consumer.** `converge_formatter_exclusion` (`intentsvcs/src/facade.rs`) appends `Project::generated_view_patterns` to a consumer's `.prettierignore`, so that a formatter never becomes a second writer of generated views (AC-07.6). Its patterns cover issue views (`intent/issues/*.md`) and the whiteboard's board and inbox views.
- **It has two callers: `intent init` (`init.rs:503`) and the last act of the v2 migration inside `Facade::upgrade` (`facade.rs:2909`).** A consumer that migrated before the function existed, or before its pattern list grew to issue and whiteboard views, never receives it, and no later verb converges it. `intent upgrade` has no report mode and reaches the call only while migrating, and `intent claude upgrade` does not call it. This is derived from the code; `intent upgrade` was not run in Utilz.
- **Nothing reports the gap.** Utilz's `.prettierignore` holds two patterns, `intent/st/**` and `intent/todo.md`, hand-written in August from the rationale Intent's own tree uses. `intent doctor --verbose` in Utilz gives no finding and no advisory about the exclusion. So Utilz's issue and whiteboard views have been open to the formatter since they became rendered views, with nothing saying so. That is the failure `converge_formatter_exclusion`'s own doc comment describes: the estate that fixed itself by hand stopped being able to see the bug, and the consumer stayed exposed.
- **The hook order lets the rewrite land.** `insert_chain_block` puts Intent's chain after the hook's shebang and `set` preamble, ahead of the consumer's own blocks. So the guards, the critic gate and the doctor gate all run before a consumer block that rewrites and re-stages files. The rewrite reaches the commit unchecked, and the next commit's gate is the first to see it, where it refuses everything rather than only the file that drifted.
- **The renderer passes a stored body through as it is.** A body that is not formatter-stable, here a doubled blank line, yields a view a formatter changes. 0110 settled the same class for `AGENTS.md`: the renderer's output must be prettier-stable rather than excepted. Stored issue bodies are the same class on another artefact.

## A second consequence of the same hook: a path-scoped commit leaves the index stale

Nodes on a shared tree commit by explicit path (`git commit -- <paths>`) so as not to sweep a peer's staged files into their commit. For such a commit git runs the hook against a temporary index, so the formatter's `git add` lands there. The commit carries the formatted file while the real index keeps the pre-format text, and the next plain commit reverts the formatting. utilz-cc found it; utilz-vc reproduced it in a scratch repository with Utilz's hook block verbatim (git 2.55.0, prettier 3.9.6):

```
git commit -- a.md          blank lines -- HEAD: 2  index: 3  worktree: 2
                            git status --short  ->  MM a.md
git add a.md; git commit    blank lines -- HEAD: 2  index: 2  worktree: 2, status clean
```

This is 0179's shape, a private-index commit leaving the ambient index stale, from a third trigger, and 0179's repair covers it: `git restore --staged -- <every committed path>` after the commit. Intent's own tree cannot hit it, because its gate checks the staged blob and never rewrites (0263). A consumer that keeps a rewriting block can.

## What a fix has to give, none of it ruled

- A consumer that migrated before the exclusion existed gets it: either a verb that converges it again, such as `intent upgrade` on a current project or `intent claude upgrade`, or a doctor finding that names each missing pattern.
- When `intent doctor` reports a skew whose diff is a formatter's (a collapsed blank-line run, or `*x*` become `_x_`), it says a formatter is the likely second writer rather than presenting the drift as a hand-edit.
- Stored bodies render formatter-stable, carrying 0110's principle from `AGENTS.md` to issue bodies. Or `issues add` and `issues edit` refuse a body whose render a formatter would change.
- Optionally, when `intent claude upgrade` inserts the chain into a hook with a later block that rewrites and re-stages staged files, it says so.

Noticed on the way: `generated_view_patterns`'s doc comment speaks of five patterns, four of them derived, and the function returns eight. The doc comment on `converge_formatter_exclusion` also says it writes five.

## In Utilz

`895a2fc` fixed the three bodies. Utilz is adding the eight generated-view patterns to its own `.prettierignore` under its own issue, in the block `converge_formatter_exclusion` would write, so a later converge changes nothing there.

CLOSED 2026-09-14 18:45Z: Closed on (a) and (b), as vc ruled. (a) `intent claude upgrade --apply`, the verb a consumer takes canon by, now converges the formatter exclusion through Facade::claude_upgrade and names each generated-view pattern it adds to `.prettierignore` (a dry run names what it would add), so a consumer that took canon before the exclusion covered issue and whiteboard views gets the rest; doctor stays out of it. (b) When doctor's view-skew diff is one a formatter makes, a collapsed blank-line run or `*x*` become `_x_` (views::differs_as_a_formatter_would), the finding says a formatter is the likely second writer and names the converge; a hand edit is not blamed on one. The doc comments on generated_view_patterns and converge_formatter_exclusion no longer count patterns. (c) is left open: whether stored bodies should render formatter-stable, carrying 0110's principle from AGENTS.md to issue bodies, is a separate question to file if anyone wants it. (d), a warning when the chain lands ahead of a consumer block that rewrites and re-stages, is out. Fixed in the commit that closes this issue.
